perf.summary: Branchy mirror init and redundant null-window guard; the i<=r test is subsumed by l<=r when r is the active window, and Math.Min reads d[] then branches.
perf.currentCost: Per i: ternary l<=r && i<=r ? Math.Min(d[l+r-i], r-i+1) : 1. Two comparisons plus a Math.Min (which on int is a compare+cmov but Burst may emit a branch). The l<=r check is loop-invariant-ish but evaluated every iteration; mirror index l+r-i is recomputed.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist int center = l + r into nothing useful but instead: since r starts at -1 and only grows, replace l<=r with a single r>=i test after ensuring r initialized; compute int k = i <= r ? Math.Min(d[l + r - i], r - i + 1) : 1; (the l<=r is implied because whenever r>=0 we have l<=r by construction). This drops one comparison per iteration on the hot O(n) loop.
perf.rationale: Removes one branch from every iteration of the linear scan. The invariant l<=r holds whenever r>=0 because (l,r) are only assigned together as a valid window, so testing only i<=r is sufficient and equivalent.
perf.risk: Must verify the window invariant l<=r holds at all r>=0 (it does: l=i-k, r=i+k with k>=1 in Odd so l<=r). If r==-1, i<=r is false so the else branch (1) is taken, matching original. Equivalent.

perf.summary: Same redundant l<=r guard as Odd; drop to single i<=r comparison.
perf.currentCost: Per i: l<=r && i<=r ? Math.Min(d[l+r-i+1], r-i+1) : 0 evaluates two comparisons every iteration.
perf.proposedChange: int k = i <= r ? Math.Min(d[l + r - i + 1], r - i + 1) : 0; relying on the window invariant l<=r whenever r>=0. Saves one comparison per iteration.
perf.rationale: Identical reasoning to Odd: (l,r) are assigned together as a valid window so l<=r is implied by r>=0; removing the redundant test shortens the per-iteration critical path of the O(n) scan.
perf.risk: For Even, k can be 0 so l=i-k-1 = i-1, r=i+k=i; l<=r holds (i-1<=i). When r==-1 the else (0) is taken. Equivalent — verify the d[l+r-i+1] index stays in-bounds, which it does because i<=r implies the mirror index is within [l,r].

perf.summary: Math.Min(int,int) may not be recognized by Burst as branchless; use math.min or manual cmov pattern.
perf.currentCost: Math.Min from System.Math; under Burst the System.Math.Min(int,int) intrinsic is usually fine but not guaranteed to vectorize/branchless across versions, and pulling System.Math into a Burst hot path is less idiomatic than Unity.Mathematics math.min.
perf.proposedChange: If Unity.Mathematics is available in this module, use math.min(a,b) which Burst lowers to a branchless min. Otherwise replace with a manual branchless form: int m = b + ((a - b) & ((a - b) >> 31)); for a<b style min (with care on overflow). Keep Math.Min if it already lowers to cmov.
perf.rationale: Guarantees branchless min in the hot O(n) inner expression, avoiding a potential mispredicted branch per character.
perf.risk: Manual branchless min can overflow on a-b for extreme int ranges; here both operands are bounded by n (string length) so a-b cannot overflow. Prefer math.min to avoid the overflow caveat entirely.
